cards.title: Redirect early creative feedback toward problem solving
cards.claim: During idea generation, reframing objections as modification questions can avoid immediately shutting down an idea.
cards.action: Instead of saying "That's too expensive" or "That'll never pass legal," ask how the idea could be made less expensive or how wording could be modified to be legally available.
applies_when: A team is generating names or other creative concepts
Someone is inclined to reject an idea immediately because of cost or legal concerns
do_not_use_when: The team has explicitly moved into its elimination or evaluation stage
unknowns: Whether this approach improves creative output for a particular team
How long the non-evaluative period should last
evidence_quotes: "I wish we could make that so it wasn't expensive." Or, "How do we how do we modify that word so it's legally available?"
"What you've done there is you've given someone a problem-solving proposition. you haven't slammed a a name down."
"there's a certain point where you know you you do start just eliminating things"

cards.title: Review naming directions after two working cycles
cards.claim: The described naming process uses about two cycles, or two to two and a half weeks, before reviewing progress against a creative framework and potentially sending candidates to legal.
cards.action: After about two cycles, review the work against the creative framework; if it is ready, send it to legal.
applies_when: A naming project has gone through initial exploration cycles
Team members are balancing the project with several other assignments
Names may need legal review across multiple markets
do_not_use_when: The work has not yet completed the initial exploratory cycles
There is no defined creative framework or legal-review requirement
unknowns: What qualifies a set of names as ready for legal review
Whether the two-to-two-and-a-half-week timing applies to other team sizes or workloads
evidence_quotes: "But after we've gone through really about two cycles, which is a two two and a half week period because people are working not on not on this one project for two and a half weeks."
"we go back and we look now at the objectives. We call it the creative framework."
"Hey, I think we're I think we're getting there. Let's ship this off to legal."

cards.title: Use unfamiliar reading for a late-stage creative perspective
cards.claim: A suggested pre-final-draft exercise is to spend 30 minutes with unfamiliar magazines or a book and look for seemingly unrelated connections that could inform the work.
cards.action: Before the final draft, read a couple of magazines you have never read before for 30 minutes and look for connections that could be moved into the project.
applies_when: Developing a final draft for a fiber-related article or analogous creative project
Seeking a new perspective or spin before finalizing work
do_not_use_when: The work requires immediate completion without time for exploratory reading
The team needs validated evidence rather than speculative creative connections
unknowns: Whether the stated frequency of finding a useful perspective is reproducible
How to evaluate whether an imported connection is appropriate for the project
evidence_quotes: "I would go to a bookstore and I would either get a book or it'd be easier to get a couple magazines that you never have read before"
"I would spend 30 minutes on those two magazines just looking for connections that might be moved into your article."
"you got to suspend logic and evaluation and just speculate"
